stories.title: Now that the 53 is set, predict the Bills win total (2026 Edition)
stories.summary:
Now that we know the initial 53-man roster, and the practice squad is set, it's prediction time.  This is the time every year that I make my one (1) prediction for the Bills regular season.  My track record is pretty good - I'm generally +/- 1 win from the Bills' actual total.  (Last year I hit it exact.)



	 



	I don't go game-by-game; instead I try to look holistically at the Bills as a team for the full season.  I do take overall strength of schedule into account, but upsets happen both ways, so I think it's futile to predict the results of each week well in advance.  Likewise, injuries happen, guys have big games here and there, etc.  There's some averaging out, but overall a really good team tends to win more than a fairly good team, which tends to win more than a mediocre team, and so on.



	 



	So with that preamble aside, I'll go on record:  I'm predicting 12 wins from the Bills this year.  I have way better vibes going in to this season, but the new players and schemes will need some time to gel, and the schedule is very tough.

stories.title: New Season. Fresh Optimism.
stories.summary:
This will be my one and only thread devoted to how I feel about the 2026 season. 
	 



	I don’t over- or under-value my contributions to this forum, but anyone who has read my comments over the years knows I’m an optimist. Some claim I work for Bills PR. I assure you I don’t. I’m simply a reasonably intelligent, lifelong Bills fan who looks for the silver lining rather than the storm cloud. I’ll never profess to be an X’s and O’s guy or evaluator of film, but I’ve watched a hell of a lot of football over the years and learned a lot from reading opinions on this very board. 



	 



	The 2026 season has me more “juiced” than any since 2021. Although some have bemoaned the promotion of Brady and retention of Beane as ill-advised, I’ll go ahead and say I think this is the best roster of the Beane era. I believe this offense has the potential to break records and crush opponents’ spirit. We’re talking 2007 Pats*** level — with a more satisfying ending. 
	 



	I predict that Joe Brady is going to really impress people who thought Pegula did the “easy” thing by promoting him. I have read multiple reports this preseason that there is a new and different energy around camp. Micah Hyde just said so on the Buffalo Plus podcast yesterday, based solely upon what players have told him.



	 



	The Bills are going to be an aggressive football team, which is what I and many others have felt was lacking in recent years. McDermott tried — he let Josh go for 4th downs at a high rate — but at the end of the day we always seemed to be a reactive team. No more.



	 



	i think Josh is refreshed, refocused, and will be on a mission no opponent can derail. He’s the best player in the league, an even better person, and he has the most talent around him in his career. 
	 



	Watch out, NFL…the Bills are coming for you. 
	 



	Go Bills!!!

I was lucky enough to be a freshman at UB and was able to attend the last game at the Rockpile. 21-21 tie against the Lions.



	The next season opened the Orchard Park stadium. The traffic was horrendous as no prior, proper, planning had occurred. Buses of all types were stalled on the I-90 with passengers running to the bushes to answer nature’s call.

Vince Young Documentary on Netflix
stories.summary:
Watched the Vince Young Documentary on Netflix.....actually forgot he was on the Bills roster for a hot minute.



	 



	Obviously he was super talented, and he seems to have a decent level of intelligence......but as you will see when you watch it, what he lacked was emotional toughness.



	 



	One person who came off pretty bad in the Doc was Coach Jeff Fisher.



	 



	I believe Barry Switzer once said the most important job for a Coach is to figure out which players need a kick in the butt, and which players need a pat on the back, and act accordingly.



	 



	Vince Young seemed to be a player that needed a pat on the back, but all he got from Fisher were kicks in the butt.



	 



	Sad that Young seemed to have all the physical tools and intelligence to be great, but if you look into his family history and his behavior in his early days at Texas, any decent GM should've been able to spot the red flags that would lead you to believe he wouldn't be able to cut it on the Pro level.

	Since then, he's missed both Pre-Season games, the scrimmage against the Browns, and the Bills 2nd scrimmage practice at the stadium. Which is very important development time for a Rookie.

	87. Tetairoa McMillan, WR, Panthers



	86. Tuli Tuipulotu, LB, Chargers



	85. Brock Purdy, QB, 49ers



	 



	Bryce Young?!? If I were Nelson or Jordan, I'd be a little PO'ed.



	 



	Update 7/1:



	In addition to Bryce Young, seems the Panthers are getting a lot of love with McMillan making the list at 87.



	Purdy coming in at 85 is getting a lot of chatter. He definitely belongs above Bryce Young, but do either really belong?



	 



	Update 9/1:



	https://www.nfl.com/news/top-100-players-of-2026-nos-10-1



	 



	#3 Bijan Robinson.



	Still no Josh or Myles Garrett so playing out like we thought. Great to see our boy get the respect.
